title: Telemetry rewrites its 4 MB runtime summary file on every event

root_cause_analysis.telemetry_persist_cost: RuntimeSummaryProjectionStore.project_event() and _reject_binding_reclaim() in services/telemetry/runtime_summary.py called self._persist() on every projected event. _persist() serialized all runtime summaries via json.dumps(self._summaries, indent=2, sort_keys=True) into a temporary file (runtime_summaries.json.<uuid>.tmp) and atomically replaced runtime_summaries.json. With a ~4.06 MB runtime_summaries.json and ~203 ingest events/min (~3.38 events/s), telemetry serialized and wrote ~4.06 MB 3.38 times per second (~13.7 MB/s write_bytes and ~0.63 CPU core on the background asyncio loop thread). Additionally, if the process was killed mid-write, orphaned runtime_summaries.json.<uuid>.tmp files remained on disk.

non_trading_saturday_203_ingest_calls_pe.explanation: Continuous heartbeat emission on a non-trading Saturday is expected by design so active paper runtime bindings do not exceed TELEMETRY_RUNTIME_HEARTBEAT_STALE_SECONDS (default 90s) and degrade on weekends. However, the observed ~203 POST /api/telemetry/ingest calls/min (~3.38/s across the active paper runtime processes managed by paper-fleet-reconciler) is higher than the configured PANTHEON_RUNTIME_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_SECONDS=15.0s cadence because in services/execution/lean_runtime/paper_runtime.py, _run_loop() invokes drain_once() every PANTHEON_RUNTIME_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS (default 1.0s, lines 5202-5205 and 5592-5595), and drain_once() unconditionally calls _maybe_emit_heartbeat() (line 5335) even when 0 signals were drained. _maybe_emit_heartbeat() (lines 6340-6342) only deduplicates within the same whole UTC second (if self._last_heartbeat_at == now: return) instead of checking elapsed time against heartbeat_interval_seconds. Per task brief instructions, the ingest rate of paper-fleet-reconciler / paper_runtime and the BFF downstream health monitor was not modified in this task.

fix_summary.persistence_design: Replaced per-event full file rewrites in RuntimeSummaryProjectionStore with an append-only, fsync-backed delta journal (runtime_summaries.json.delta.jsonl) and a bounded periodic full checkpoint (_FULL_PERSIST_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 60.0s).
fix_summary.durability_on_202: When runtime_summaries.json already exists and the 60s full-checkpoint interval has not elapsed, _persist_summary_change() computes only the changed/removed top-level fields of the affected runtime summary and appends a compact JSONL patch record to runtime_summaries.json.delta.jsonl followed by os.fsync(fd) before returning from project_event(), guaranteeing that every HTTP 202 acknowledgement survives SIGKILL.
fix_summary.startup_and_graceful_shutdown_compatibil: On startup (_load()), RuntimeSummaryProjectionStore cleans up any orphaned runtime_summaries.json.*.tmp files, loads runtime_summaries.json, replays any pending records from runtime_summaries.json.delta.jsonl, and folds them into runtime_summaries.json. On graceful stop (RuntimeSummaryProjectionStore.flush()/close(), atexit hook, and services/telemetry/main.py shutdown() + SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers), any pending delta journal is folded into runtime_summaries.json with exact indent=2, sort_keys=True formatting and the .delta.jsonl file is unlinked, leaving runtime_summaries.json 100% readable by the previous telemetry version.

local_benchmark_4mb_store.store_shape: 23 runtimes x 8 TW symbols built from frozen hosted _REAL_D551_SUMMARY with full Taiwan official market mark_lineage (50 content_refs, 50 source_ids, 11 ingest_run_ids per symbol), calendar_evidence, positions, _cost_by_symbol, last_lifecycle_identity, recent_lifecycle_event_ids, and order_execution_observations (4,123,890 bytes serialized).

ac_1_no_per_event_full_rewrite_and_bound.proof: 300 real-shaped events projected over a 60s window against a 4.12 MB store performed 1 full rewrite at the 60s boundary and 299 compact delta appends.

ac_2_202_updates_survive_sigkill_and_res.proof: Subprocess running services.telemetry.main received a burst of 24 ingest events (all HTTP 202), was immediately killed with SIGKILL, and on restart recovered 100% of acknowledged updates from runtime_summaries.json + runtime_summaries.json.delta.jsonl while cleaning up orphaned .tmp files.

ac_3_exact_path_format_and_previous_vers.proof: After SIGTERM graceful stop of services.telemetry.main, runtime_summaries.json remained at its exact path with indent=2, sort_keys=True formatting, no .delta.jsonl or .tmp files remained, and the previous telemetry version's _load() implementation read every update identically.

ac_4_identical_reads_and_bff_responses_o.proof: Across heartbeats, trade_decision, paper_fill_simulated, pnl_snapshot with mark_refs, and binding reclaim rejection on the 4.12 MB store, project_event(), get(), list(), GET /api/telemetry/runtime-summaries, and GET /api/telemetry/runtime-summaries/<runtime_id> matched the legacy per-event full-rewrite store byte-for-byte.

ac_5_local_measurement_cpu_below_0_1_cor.proof: Measured before (0.2454-0.2957 CPU cores, 13.15 MB/s writes) vs after (0.0748-0.0832 CPU cores < 0.1 core, 0.0488 MB/s writes < 0.5 MB/s).

ac_6_no_new_endpoint_service_db_or_env_a.proof: Zero new endpoints, services, databases, or environment variables added. Full services/telemetry pytest suite passed (524 passed, 1 skipped, 54 subtests passed).

ac_7_no_existing_test_weakened_or_delete.proof: No existing test file was modified, weakened, or deleted.
